## The problem

Our team of twelve has drifted into a pattern of long-lived feature branches that often survive for two to three weeks before merging. What looked like a way to isolate risk has instead created the opposite: integration pain that grows with every day a branch stays open. Merge conflicts have become routine, code review happens on stale diffs that no longer reflect main, and we regularly discover that two branches touched the same module in incompatible ways only after both are "done." Last month's payments refactor took four extra days purely to resolve conflicts that had nothing to do with the actual feature. We are spending real engineering time paying interest on delayed integration, and it is getting worse as the team grows.

## The proposal

I propose we move to trunk-based development: everyone commits small, frequent changes directly to main (or through branches that live less than a day), gated by feature flags for anything incomplete.

- Adopt feature flags so unfinished work can sit in main without being user-visible.
- Require CI to pass before any merge, with a hard rule that main is always deployable.
- Set a team norm that branches older than one day get merged or abandoned.

This shrinks the size of every merge, surfaces conflicts within hours instead of weeks, and makes code review faster because diffs are small and current.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is real: trunk-based development demands stronger discipline around testing and feature-flag hygiene, and if our CI suite has gaps, we could ship broken code to main more often, not less. This is a legitimate risk, not a strawman — a team with flaky or slow tests will feel more pain under this model, not less, because there's no branch to hide failures in. The honest answer is that we need to invest in CI reliability and flag cleanup before flipping the switch, not after.

- Budget two weeks of CI hardening as a prerequisite, not an afterthought.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
